summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT). Experienced in embedded firmware in bare-metal C across STM32 Cortex-M4, Raspberry Pi, and Arduino platforms — UART, I2C, ADC, PWM, and interrupt-driven peripheral control. Validated systems using Proteus simulation, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers; version-controlled all firmware with Git.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi Pico and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID cursor commands via firmware in Python.
Implemented a tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter via software calibration and ADC resolution tuning.
Produced full technical documentation including claims write-up and BOM for an AI-based Mixed Reality headset concept.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE; implemented UART and I2C sensor communication with closed-loop feedback for national-level competition robots.
Led a 25-member team end-to-end across firmware development, PCB fabrication, and system integration for national robotics competitions.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Built a PyQt GUI for real-time laboratory data acquisition; used GitLab for version control and technical documentation — equivalent workflow to Git + issue tracking.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed STM32 Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C: GPIO, TIM2 timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C display driver.
Achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified full peripheral behavior in Proteus simulation.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control on STM32 with interrupt-driven UART command reception and user override; coordinated UART, I2C (VL53L0X ToF), and OLED tasks under FreeRTOS with mutex-protected shared memory.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos via PWM with range-gated contact detection using dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over TCA9548A I2C multiplexer.
Resolved 11 integration failures (servo crosstalk, I2C contention, false-positive detections); achieved 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
